newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa a touch lower, conditions thin.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa a touch lower, conditions thin.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures were a touch lower by Thursday midssion but conditions were subdued as the market paused to consolidate the recent gains, traders said.
But given an encouraging technical outlook, cocoa was still vulnerable to further upside moves, they said.
"It's more likely to go higher," said one. But any rise, like in previous sessions, was unlikely to be backed by heavy volume, they said.

Cocoa was called unchanged to three stg down on numbers. The market gapped a couple of sterling higher but later retraced to end the midsession about unchanged to six down save for the expiring July contract.
September was unchanged at 1,024 stg a tonne after absorbing light selling. Traders said they were still looking for a test through 1,030-1,035 on September following this week's high of 1,028.
The initial support stood firm at 1,000 stg.
Overall volume was a tiny 876 lots.
Traders said news the International Cocoa Organisation (ICCO) raised this season's cocoa deficit to 134,000 tonnes from its earlier estimate of 115,000 had no impact.
Also, the overnight news of the routine ICCO buffer stock sale on Thursday had probably been digested.
The ICCO said the higher cocoa deficit estimate reflected a 20,000-tonne cut in its crop forecast to 2.695 million. There was basically no change in the grinding estimate of 2.80 million.
